data.summary: The pod startup breached its 10.0-second SLO, taking 30.0 seconds to become Ready. This was primarily due to a slow image pull, which consumed 28.724 seconds of the total startup time. The image was pulled at a rate of 1.85 MB/s, significantly below the 5 MB/s threshold for normal throughput.

findings.statement: The pod startup took 30.0 seconds, exceeding the SLO of 10.0 seconds.
The image_pull phase was the dominant factor, lasting 28.724 seconds.
The image size was 53,328,919 bytes (approximately 53 MB).
The image pull throughput was 1,856,598 bytes/s (approximately 1.85 MB/s).
This throughput is below the 5 MB/s threshold identified as normal in the detector findings and the slow_registry runbook.

ruled_out.reason: The image pull was slow due to low throughput (1.85 MB/s), not because the image size alone made a normal pull long. The definition of 'large_image' implies normal pull throughput.
The 'model_s' signal indicates 0.0 seconds spent on model loading.
The 'app_init' phase took only 1.689 seconds, which is a minor portion of the total startup time and well within the SLO.
The 'scheduling' phase duration was 0.0 seconds, and there were no failed scheduling events.
The 'readiness' phase duration was 0.0 seconds, and there were no probe failures after the application was ready.

recommendations.rationale: Pre-pulling the image can prevent scale-up from being dependent on registry throughput, as suggested by the slow_registry runbook.

recommendations.action: Advisory: use a registry mirror or pull-through cache close to the cluster; check registry rate limits.
recommendations.rationale: Improving the network path to the registry or mitigating rate limits can increase image pull throughput, as recommended by the slow_registry runbook.
